items.stem: Distinguish between shares and debentures on any six bases.
items.answer: (i) Return: shares: dividend, paid out of profits; debentures: interest at a fixed rate, payable even if there is no profit. (ii) Issue at discount: shares: shares cannot be issued at a discount (except sweat equity); debentures: can be issued at a discount. (iii) Voting rights: shares: equity shareholders have voting rights; debentures: no voting rights. (iv) Repayment: shares: not repaid during the life of the company (except buy-back/redemption of preference shares); debentures: repaid after a fixed period. (v) Security: shares: not secured; debentures: generally secured by a charge on assets. (vi) Convertibility: shares: shares cannot be converted into debentures; debentures: debentures can be converted into shares.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis (any six relevant bases): (i) Return: shares: dividend, paid out of profits; debentures: interest at a fixed rate, payable even if there is no profit. (ii) Issue at discount: shares: shares cannot be issued at a discount (except sweat equity); debentures: can be issued at a discount. (iii) Voting rights: shares: equity shareholders have voting rights; debentures: no voting rights. (iv) Repayment: shares: not repaid during the life of the company (except buy-back/redemption of preference shares); debentures: repaid after a fixed period. (v) Security: shares: not secured; debentures: generally secured by a charge on assets. (vi) Convertibility: shares: shares cannot be converted into debentures; debentures: debentures can be converted into shares.

items.stem:
Malhotra Retail Ltd needs ₹5 crore for expansion. Manish, its finance manager, compares issuing equity shares with issuing 9% debentures. The company has stable profits and its owners do not want to dilute control.
(i) Which option suits the owners' wish? Give two reasons. (ii) State one risk of choosing debentures.
items.answer: (i) Debentures: debenture holders have no voting rights, so control is not diluted; interest is tax-deductible and the cost is fixed. (ii) Interest must be paid even in a loss year and the principal must be repaid; a charge on assets is created.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Debentures: debenture holders have no voting rights, so control is not diluted; interest is tax-deductible and the cost is fixed. (ii) Interest must be paid even in a loss year and the principal must be repaid; a charge on assets is created.
